minutes.summary: The Select Board met from 5:37 p.m. to interview three finalists for town manager in turn: a candidate from Fair Haven, one from West Boylston, and the Holden public works director. Each candidate answered the same set of questions and gave a mock town meeting presentation. The board said it would be in touch with candidates next. No decision on who to hire was made in the captions.

what_happened.line: The Select Board interviewed three town manager finalists in turn, from Fair Haven, West Boylston and the Holden public works director; no vote was taken.
Each candidate gave a mock town meeting presentation: an override presentation, an MBTA zoning presentation, and a road project presentation.
The Fair Haven candidate described a deficit and a failed override in her prior town, and how it was handled with cuts and a trash fee.
The West Boylston candidate noted that a new manager would deliver a mid-February budget built by others, in a town just off an override.
The board told the last candidate it would be letting him know next; no selection was announced.

why_it_matters: The town manager prepares and presents the annual budget, so whoever is chosen will shape the next budget cycle and any future override question residents are asked to vote on.
The candidates' remarks on overrides, new growth splits and multi-year planning are statements of approach from past roles, not Lunenburg decisions.
